title: Articulatory gestures as phonological units
significance: Argued phonological primitives are coordinated vocal-tract gestures, not abstract static symbols!

title: The motor theory of speech perception revised
significance: A full-scale defense and update of motor theory, decades after the original 1967 proposal.

title: Acoustic Phonetics
significance: The definitive modern textbook directly linking articulation to acoustic output.

title: Acoustical consequences of lip, tongue, jaw, and larynx movement
significance: Modeled how individual articulators shape the acoustic vowel space.

title: Speech sound acquisition, coarticulation, and rate effects in a neural network model of speech production
significance: Introduced the DIVA model linking neural control directly to articulatory movement.

title: Speaking: From Intention to Articulation
significance: The landmark book-length model of how speakers turn thoughts into articulated words.

title: A spreading-activation theory of retrieval in sentence production
significance: Modeled speech errors as activation spreading through an interactive lexical network.

title: A theory of lexical access in speech production
significance: Integrated decades of speech-error and chronometric evidence into one processing model.

title: The analysis of sentence production
significance: An early, highly influential account of the stages underlying sentence planning.

title: Categorical perception: Issues, methods, findings
significance: A comprehensive early review that shaped decades of categorical perception research.

title: Speech perception by the chinchilla: Voiced-voiceless distinction in alveolar plosive consonants
significance: Chinchillas show the same VOT boundary as humans — a landmark for the auditory account of categorical perception!

title: Auditory and phonetic memory codes in the discrimination of consonants and vowels
significance: Distinguished short-lived auditory memory from more durable phonetic memory in perception.

title: The influence of the lexicon on phonetic decision making
significance: Showed real-word knowledge can shift exactly where listeners place a phoneme category boundary.

title: Merging information in speech recognition: Feedback is never necessary
significance: A provocative target article arguing lexical feedback to phoneme perception isn't needed at all.

title: Speech perception without speaker normalization: An exemplar model
significance: Proposed listeners store detailed talker-specific traces rather than normalizing them away.

title: Influence of vocalic context on perception of the [sh]-[s] distinction
significance: Early evidence that listeners perceptually compensate for coarticulation from neighboring sounds.

title: Der aphasische Symptomencomplex
significance: Proposed a dual-center model of language in the brain that still anchors aphasiology today.

title: The organization of language and the brain
significance: Synthesized the classic disconnection-syndrome model of aphasia for a broad audience.

title: Phonetic feature encoding in human superior temporal gyrus
significance: Direct cortical recordings revealed phonetic features mapped across the human STG.

title: Functional neuroimaging of speech perception in infants
significance: Showed infant brains already engage adult-like left-hemisphere speech regions.

title: Hierarchical processing in spoken language comprehension
significance: Mapped how the brain moves from acoustic analysis to meaning across a cortical hierarchy.

title: Of human bonding: Newborns prefer their mothers' voices
significance: Newborns already recognize mom's voice — language learning starts in the womb!

title: A precursor of language acquisition in young infants
significance: Four-day-olds distinguish their native language from a foreign one by rhythm alone.

title: Linguistic experience alters phonetic perception in infants by 6 months of age
significance: Showed native-language vowel categories begin reshaping perception in the first half-year of life.

title: Infant sensitivity to distributional information can affect phonetic discrimination
significance: Brief exposure to a statistical distribution of sounds retunes infant phoneme discrimination.

title: Phonological Development: The Origins of Language in the Child
significance: A comprehensive account of how babbling matures into a first language's sound system.

title: Bilingualism in Development: Language, Literacy, and Cognition
significance: A comprehensive account of how growing up bilingual reshapes language and cognitive development.

title: Continuous speech recognition by statistical methods
significance: Set out the statistical blueprint ASR systems followed for the next three decades.

title: A maximum likelihood approach to continuous speech recognition
significance: Formalized the maximum-likelihood framework underlying HMM-based speech recognizers.

title: Minimum prediction residual principle applied to speech recognition
significance: Introduced the Itakura distance, a core metric for comparing speech spectra.

title: Dynamic programming algorithm optimization for spoken word recognition
significance: Introduced dynamic time warping, the classic algorithm for aligning speech of different lengths.

title: Distance measures for speech recognition, psychological and instrumental
significance: Compared perceptually-motivated distance metrics — a direct precursor to the MFCC.

title: Signal estimation from modified short-time Fourier transform
significance: The Griffin-Lim algorithm for recovering a waveform from a spectrogram — still used in TTS vocoders today!

title: Speech recognition with deep recurrent neural networks
significance: Showed deep LSTMs could push phoneme recognition to then-record accuracy.

title: Listen, Attend and Spell
significance: An attention-based encoder-decoder that recognizes speech without a separate pronunciation model.

title: Deep Speech 2: End-to-end speech recognition in English and Mandarin
significance: Scaled end-to-end ASR across two very different languages with a single architecture.

title: Attention-based models for speech recognition
significance: Brought the attention mechanism from machine translation into end-to-end speech recognition.

title: SpecAugment: A simple data augmentation method for automatic speech recognition
significance: A deceptively simple spectrogram-masking trick that became standard ASR training practice.

title: Natural TTS synthesis by conditioning WaveNet on mel spectrogram predictions
significance: Tacotron 2 paired a sequence-to-sequence acoustic model with a neural vocoder for near-human TTS.

title: FastSpeech: Fast, robust and controllable text to speech
significance: Ditched autoregression for parallel TTS generation hundreds of times faster than before.

title: HiFi-GAN: Generative adversarial networks for efficient and high fidelity speech synthesis
significance: A GAN vocoder generating high-fidelity audio dramatically faster than autoregressive models.

title: WaveGlow: A flow-based generative network for speech synthesis
significance: Combined flow-based generative modeling with a WaveNet-style architecture for fast, parallel audio synthesis.

title: Parallel WaveGAN: A fast waveform generation model based on generative adversarial networks with multi-resolution spectrogram
significance: A lightweight GAN vocoder enabling real-time, high-quality speech synthesis on-device.

title: Conditional variational autoencoder with adversarial learning for end-to-end text-to-speech
significance: VITS fused the acoustic model and vocoder into one end-to-end generative TTS system.

title: HuBERT: Self-supervised speech representation learning by masked prediction of hidden units
significance: Learned powerful speech representations by predicting clustered hidden units from masked audio.

title: data2vec: A general framework for self-supervised learning in speech, vision and language
significance: One self-supervised recipe unifying speech, vision, and text representation learning.

title: Libri-light: A benchmark for ASR with limited or no supervision
significance: Released 60,000 hours of unlabeled speech that powered the self-supervised speech boom.

title: High fidelity neural audio compression
significance: EnCodec's discrete audio tokens became the backbone representation for today's generative speech models.

title: Neural codec language models are zero-shot text to speech synthesizers
significance: VALL-E treats TTS as language modeling over audio codec codes — cloning a voice from 3 seconds of audio!

title: AudioLM: a language modeling approach to audio generation
significance: Generated coherent speech, and even piano continuations, purely by predicting the next audio token.

title: Voicebox: Text-guided multilingual universal speech generation at scale
significance: A single flow-matching model handles zero-shot TTS, editing, denoising, and more, across six languages.

title: SeamlessM4T: Massively multilingual & multimodal machine translation
significance: One model for speech-to-speech, speech-to-text, and text translation across up to 100 languages.

title: The meaning of intonational contours in the interpretation of discourse
significance: Linked specific pitch-accent and boundary-tone combinations to discourse meaning.

title: ToBI: A standard for labeling English prosody
significance: Established the ToBI annotation system still used to transcribe English intonation.

title: Suprasegmentals
significance: A foundational book-length treatment of stress, length, and pitch above the segment.

title: The Social Differentiation of English in Norwich
significance: A landmark quantitative study linking pronunciation variants to social class and gender.

title: Linguistic Variation as Social Practice
significance: Showed how Detroit high schoolers use sound change to perform social identity, not just mark it.

title: Language and Social Networks
significance: Explained sound change through the strength of speakers' everyday social-network ties.

title: Natural language and natural selection
significance: Argued language is an adaptation shaped by natural selection, sparking decades of debate.

title: The Faculty of Language: What Is It, Who Has It, and How Did It Evolve?
significance: Distinguished a narrow, uniquely-human language faculty from broader shared cognitive capacities.
